definition: VideoPoet is a large language model developed by Google Research in 2023 for video making.
details: It can be asked to animate still images. The model accepts text, images, and videos as inputs, with a program to add feature for any input to any format generated content. VideoPoet was publicly announced on December 19, 2023. It uses an autoregressive language model.

explainer.lead: VideoPoet is a large language model developed by Google Research in 2023 for video making. It matters because it treats video generation as a language-modeling problem, accepting text, images, and videos as inputs.

tiers.eli5: It's like a text assistant that writes video instead of words — you describe a scene and it animates it.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers prompt it with text, images, or video, and can ask it to animate a still image; a program adds features for any input-to-any-format generated content. A common pitfall is that autoregressive generation can drift over long sequences.
tiers.paperLevel: An autoregressive language model that accepts text, images, and videos as inputs and generates video; publicly announced December 19, 2023. Limits follow from autoregressive generation, where errors can accumulate over long outputs.

explainer.example: A user supplies a still photo and a text prompt, and VideoPoet animates the image into a short moving clip.
